To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CD4 T cell clones derived in this study were islet-specific and were able to transfer diabetes to nonobese diabetic ( NOD ) mice.

a CD4+ T cell clone specific for islet antigens was sufficient to accelerate the onset of diabetes in young, diabetes-prone NIDDM mice, and that the accelerated disease process in these animals was associated with the appearance of a new population of CD4 T cells that was specific for an antigen expressed on pancreatic islet cells.
a CD4 islet-specific T-cell clone is sufficient to accelerate the development of diabetes in young diabetes-prone NED mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the immunopathogenesis of insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus (IDDM), the most common form of diabetes in the young.
the study of the pathogenesis of autoimmune diabetes, a disease in which insulin-producing beta cells are selectively destroyed.
the development of an experimental animal model for the study of autoimmune disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CD4+ T cell clone is the only cell type required for the initiation of autoimmune diabetes.
the CD4+ T cell clone is able to initiate the process of diabetes in the NOD mouse.
the CD4+ T cell is a major factor in the initiation of autoimmune diabetes in the NOD mouse.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a single CD4+ T cell clone is able to induce diabetes in NOD mice.
the NOD mouse is a model for the study of autoimmune disease.
the disease is initiated by a T cell clone, and that the disease is then perpetuated by a CD4+ T cell clone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single T cell clone is capable of initiating an autoimmune disease in a susceptible animal.
the CD4 T cell clones are sufficient to initiate the process of disease development in the diabetes-proned NOD mouse.
a single clone of T cells can be sufficient to cause diabetes.
